summary: In this excerpt from a novel, Mrs. Royce tells Lexy Moran about a young woman who lives isolated three miles from Wyngate and whom Mrs. Royce saw only once, nearly three years earlier, when Dr. Quelton brought her to Wyngate as a bride during a snowstorm. Mrs. Royce claims the doctor is crazy. When Captain Grey arrives, Lexy repeats the claim, and he dismisses it as village gossip, offering to visit the house himself and return for lunch.
one_line: Lexy Moran hears villagers call Dr. Quelton crazy and learns of an isolated young bride, and Captain Grey offers to investigate.
key_facts: Mrs. Royce says a young woman lives alone three miles from Wyngate and sees no one from one month's end to another.
Mrs. Royce describes the young woman as young and as pretty as a picture.
Mrs. Royce saw the young woman once, the night the doctor brought her to Wyngate as a young bride, about three years earlier.
The night Mrs. Royce saw her, a terrible snowstorm prevented the doctor from getting out to his place, so he brought her to Wyngate.
The young bride sat in the same room at Wyngate where Lexy is sitting.
Mrs. Royce says Dr. Quelton is crazy and that she is not the only one to say so.
The doctor says he went out to telephone and tells Lexy that Muriel has no telephone in the house.
Lexy tells Captain Grey that Dr. Quelton is crazy, as Mrs. Royce has said.
Captain Grey suppresses a smile and says that in little villages anyone out of the ordinary is called crazy.
Captain Grey offers to walk three miles to pay a call on Dr. Quelton and return to Wyngate for lunch.
Lexy says she does not think Dr. Quelton is a real physician.
Lexy had told Captain Grey she would let him help her in her little venture.
